title: Multi-Tenant AI Chatbot Widget
tagline: A secure, embeddable AI chatbot for multi-tenant websites with strict domain validation and Shadow DOM isolation.
description: A reusable chatbot widget designed for external client websites, built around single-script deployment, tenant isolation, and a lightweight integration flow.
heroSummary: A production-focused AI chatbot widget built for secure client-side embedding across multiple tenant websites, with strict origin validation, isolated rendering, and a backend that keeps sensitive logic on the server.
highlights: Single script tag deployment for fast merchant integration
Shadow DOM isolation to reduce styling conflicts and improve sandboxing
Strict domain validation to protect tenant boundaries
Backend-first security model with config and prompts kept off the client
context:
This project addresses a common product problem: businesses want to add an AI assistant to external websites without exposing internal prompts, configuration, or tenant data. The widget needed to be easy to embed, safe to operate across different merchant domains, and lightweight enough to feel like a native part of the host site.

The result is a multi-tenant chatbot widget that can be dropped into a client site with a single script tag. It is designed around secure deployment, isolation between tenants, and a clear separation between public UI configuration and server-side business logic.
problem: Build a reusable AI chatbot component that can be embedded on third-party websites while preserving tenant isolation, validating allowed domains, preventing style leakage, and keeping sensitive backend logic and data out of the browser.
architecture: Single script-tag embed flow that loads the widget with a tenant-specific storeId
Shadow DOM rendering to isolate styles from the host page
Hono backend API for configuration and chat requests
Supabase-backed data layer for tenant records and operational data
Upstash Redis for caching, session handling, and rate limiting
Strict origin and domain validation before allowing chat interactions

sections.title: Embed Flow
sections.content: Merchants integrate the widget through a single script tag that passes a store identifier. On load, the widget fetches only the safe UI configuration it needs, which keeps the integration simple while preserving the server-side boundary for sensitive data.

sections.title: Tenant Isolation
sections.content: The system is built to prevent cross-tenant leakage by validating the request origin against an allowlist of domains and by keeping system prompts and sensitive business rules on the backend. The widget also renders inside a Shadow DOM to minimize CSS collisions with the host site.

sections.title: Backend and Data Layer
sections.content: The backend is implemented with Hono and uses Supabase for persistent tenant data. Upstash Redis supports fast caching and operational controls such as session state and rate limiting, which helps keep the service responsive under normal widget traffic.

sections.title: Deployment and Operations
sections.content: The architecture separates the frontend widget and backend API so they can be deployed independently. The widget is served from Cloudflare Pages, while the API runs on Railway, giving the project a straightforward production path with clear ownership of public assets versus server logic.

challenges: Keeping the widget easy to embed without exposing sensitive tenant data — the solution was to move prompts, authorization checks, and server-side rules into the backend so the browser only receives safe configuration data.
Preventing cross-tenant access from unauthorized domains — the solution was to validate the request origin against each tenant’s allowed domain list before accepting chat traffic.
Avoiding CSS conflicts on arbitrary client websites — the solution was to render the widget in a Shadow DOM so its styles stay isolated from the host page.
Keeping the widget resilient under real-world network conditions — the solution was to add request timeouts, retry logic for config loading, runtime schema validation, and user-facing error handling.
learnings: Client-embedded products need security boundaries that are clear both in code and in deployment.
A narrow public API and server-side validation make multi-tenant systems easier to reason about.
Shadow DOM is an effective tool for preserving UI consistency on untrusted host pages.

title: KubeMind
tagline: AI-Driven Kubernetes Incident Analysis & Observability Platform
description: Final-year capstone project — an AI-powered platform that analyzes Kubernetes incidents by correlating cluster events, application logs, and resource metrics. Uses specialized AI agents to investigate failures, identify potential root causes, and generate structured incident reports and postmortems.
context: Troubleshooting Kubernetes incidents often requires engineers to investigate events, application logs, and resource metrics across different observability tools. Connecting these signals manually can be time-consuming and makes identifying the root cause of failures more difficult.
problem: How can AI agents correlate Kubernetes events, logs, and metrics to help engineers investigate incidents, identify relevant evidence, and produce actionable postmortem reports?
architecture: FastAPI backend for incident analysis and service orchestration
Kafka-based event pipeline using the kube-events topic
Prometheus for metrics collection and Loki with Promtail for log aggregation
Specialized AI agents for analyzing Kubernetes events, logs, and metrics
LangChain and LangGraph for agent orchestration, shared incident state, and cross-signal correlation
MongoDB for incident-related data and analysis results
Next.js dashboard for presenting incident investigations and reports
Docker and Minikube for containerized development and Kubernetes testing

sections.title: Kubernetes event pipeline
sections.content: Built an event-processing pipeline that captures Kubernetes events and publishes them to Kafka for downstream incident analysis. Tested against failure scenarios including CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, and OOMKilled pods.

sections.title: Multi-agent incident investigation
sections.content: Developed specialized agents to analyze logs, metrics, and Kubernetes events. Coordinated their execution through LangGraph, maintaining shared incident state and combining their findings into a unified investigation.

sections.title: Cross-signal correlation
sections.content: Implemented a correlation agent that brings together evidence from different observability signals to support incident diagnosis and help explain the context behind Kubernetes failures.

sections.title: Automated incident reporting
sections.content: Generated structured incident reports and postmortem-style summaries from the agents' findings, making investigation results easier to review and understand through the platform dashboard.

sections.title: Observability and scenario testing
sections.content: Integrated Prometheus, Loki, and Promtail to provide metrics and logs for incident analysis. Evaluated the approach across three controlled incident scenarios and compared OpenAI, Gemini, and Ollama-based models.

challenges: Correlating heterogeneous observability data — addressed through specialized agents and a correlation agent that combines findings from events, logs, and metrics.
Coordinating multi-agent investigations — addressed with LangGraph orchestration and shared incident state.
Evaluating model suitability for incident analysis — addressed by comparing OpenAI, Gemini, and Ollama across three controlled incident scenarios.
learnings: Kubernetes troubleshooting using events, logs, and resource metrics
Building multi-agent AI workflows with LangChain and LangGraph
Event-driven architecture with Kafka and observability pipelines
Designing incident investigation workflows and structured postmortem generation
Evaluating LLMs for infrastructure troubleshooting tasks

title: PromptCraft
tagline: AI-powered NFT generation and trading platform with real-time auctions
description: A full-stack NFT marketplace where users generate unique digital art via AI prompts, then list or auction their creations in real time. Features a live bidding system, wallet integration, and a GraphQL API powering both the marketplace and the generation pipeline.
context: NFT marketplaces like OpenSea require users to bring pre-generated art. PromptCraft collapses the creation and trading workflow into a single platform — you describe what you want, the AI generates it, and you can immediately list it for sale or auction.
problem: How do you build a system that keeps auction state perfectly synchronized across all connected bidders in real time, while handling the latency of AI image generation without blocking the user experience?
architecture: Vue.js 3 + Composition API frontend with the Velzon admin template
NestJS backend with modular domain architecture (auth, NFTs, auctions, wallet)
GraphQL API for marketplace queries and mutations
WebSocket gateway for real-time auction events (new bids, countdown, sold)
Server-Sent Events (SSE) for AI generation progress streaming
Python microservice wrapping the image generation model
PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM for transactional integrity on bids

sections.title: AI generation pipeline
sections.content: User submits a text prompt → NestJS sends it to the Python microservice → generation progress is streamed back via SSE so the user sees live updates → final image is stored and minted as an NFT record.

sections.title: Real-time auction system
sections.content: Each auction room is a WebSocket namespace. Bids are validated server-side (minimum increment, wallet balance, auction active) before being broadcast. A countdown timer is synchronized server-side to prevent client-side manipulation.

sections.title: GraphQL marketplace API
sections.content: All browsing, filtering, and NFT metadata queries go through GraphQL, enabling flexible front-end querying without over-fetching. Mutations (place bid, buy now, list item) go through REST for explicit error handling.

sections.title: Wallet & ownership model
sections.content: Implemented a custodial wallet model for the MVP — each user has an on-platform balance. Transfers are atomic PostgreSQL transactions to prevent double-spend on concurrent bids.

challenges: Race conditions on concurrent bids — two users submitting within milliseconds. Solved with PostgreSQL row-level locking and a server-side bid queue per auction.
AI generation taking 8-15 seconds blocking UX — solved by SSE progress streaming so the user sees the image being built, not a spinner.
Keeping WebSocket auction state consistent when a user reconnects mid-auction — solved by replaying the last N events from a server-side event log on reconnect.
learnings: Designing real-time systems with explicit consistency guarantees
SSE as a simpler alternative to WebSocket for unidirectional streaming
GraphQL schema design for a marketplace domain
